findings.title: Public control-plane onApprove silently returned HTTP 202 leaving architect ApprovalGate blocked forever
findings.detail: In src/server.ts, onApprove logged an error to stderr but returned undefined (HTTP 202 success). The Discord bot would tell the operator the approval was accepted while the architect's in-process ApprovalGate remained blocked forever, consuming API quota with no path to completion. Matched the established throw-for-daemon-only pattern already used by onVerify and onForcePr.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace console.error + implicit return with throw new Error() so dispatch() returns HTTP 500. AUDIT-IFleet-server-onApprove.

findings.title: onCancel in control-plane.ts wrote blocked state without fromState guard, overwriting terminal done/failed records
findings.detail: The onCancel handler read task state, then called store.updateState(id, 'blocked', {...}) without a fromState guard. Between the getById check and the write, the pipeline could complete and transition the task to 'done'. The unguarded write would overwrite 'done' with 'blocked'+cancelled:true, corrupting the audit trail and preventing the PR from appearing in metrics. store.updateState() already supports a fourth fromState parameter that adds WHERE state = @fromState atomically.
findings.fix_sketch: Call updateState twice (fromState='in_flight', then fromState='pending'). If neither succeeds, broadcast a warning. AUDIT-IFleet-cp-toctou.

findings.title: isAuthorAllowed compared GitHub usernames case-sensitively, silently blocking valid authors
findings.detail: src/queue/github.ts isAuthorAllowed() used Array.includes(author) with raw case. GitHub usernames are case-insensitive: the API returns 'octocat' but config might list 'OctoCAT'. A mismatch caused valid authors to be rejected silently, causing all their issues to be ignored.
findings.fix_sketch: Normalise both sides to .toLowerCase() before comparison.

findings.title: All-workers-auth-failed caused Math.min(...[Infinity]) rate-pause with unresolvable DB value and broken auto-resume
findings.detail: In checkRateLimit() (sprint.ts), when all workers had pausedUntil=Infinity (permanent auth failure), Math.min(...[Infinity])=Infinity was written to the DB as resetAt. SQLite stored it as overflow, Discord broadcast rendered 'Invalid Date', and the auto-resume check Date.now() >= Infinity was always false — the sprint could never resume. No separate event was emitted to distinguish permanent auth failure from a temporary rate pause.
findings.fix_sketch: Filter Infinity before Math.min. If all slots are non-finite, emit sprint.auth_failed event and return without pausing.

findings.title: cancelSprint could throw 'invalid sprint transition' when a task completed between allSettled and transition
findings.detail: cancelSprint() checked TERMINAL_STATES at entry, then called Promise.allSettled(cancels). During the await, a worker's task could complete and transition the sprint to 'completed' or 'failed'. The subsequent this.transition(id, {kind:'cancelled'}) would throw 'invalid sprint transition completed → cancelled', crashing the caller.
findings.fix_sketch: Re-read the sprint from store after allSettled. If state is already terminal, return the fresh record instead of calling transition().

findings.title: awaitHandle called this.now() three times per state branch producing skewed state.at, updatedAt, and emit.ts
findings.detail: In sprint.ts awaitHandle(), each switch branch called this.now() independently for state.at, updatedAt, and the emit ts field. Under a real-time clock these three timestamps could differ by up to a millisecond, making time-based queries that join across fields unreliable.
findings.fix_sketch: Capture const completedAt = this.now() once before the switch and use it for all three fields in every branch.

findings.title: runner.ts hardcoded '@monstersebas1' fallback approver — misconfiguration silently uses wrong reviewer
findings.detail: src/pipeline/runner.ts line 54 used input.approver ?? '@monstersebas1'. Factory.ts always provides approver from config, so the hardcoded fallback would only fire for misconfigured direct callers — silently assigning a specific person as reviewer with no indication the config was incomplete.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace hardcoded fallback with process.env['IFLEET_DEFAULT_APPROVER'] and throw if still absent.

findings.title: computeStructuralFingerprint called with hardcoded baseRef='main' ignoring task's configured base branch
findings.detail: In pr-decisions.ts wrapFactoryWithVerifierContext teardown, computeStructuralFingerprint() was called with baseRef: 'main' regardless of bootstrap.input.baseBranch. Tasks targeting a non-main base branch would produce fingerprints computed against the wrong base, causing incorrect structural diff comparison for dedup.

findings.title: editor commitEditorChanges used git add -A with no sensitive-path denylist check
findings.detail: src/pipeline/editor.ts commitEditorChanges() ran git add -A unconditionally, which stages every file including any .env, *.pem, *.key, or credential files that Claude tools wrote to the worktree mid-task. These would then be committed and pushed to the PR branch.
findings.fix_sketch: After git add -A, query git diff --cached --name-only -z, filter against a SENSITIVE_PATH_RE denylist, and run git restore --staged on any matches.

findings.title: Shared mutable lastCommentId in createIssueCommenter caused concurrent tasks to poll wrong comment
findings.detail: src/queue/issue-commenter.ts stored lastCommentId as a single closure-level mutable. When two concurrent tasks both called comment() then waitForApproval(), the second comment() overwrote lastCommentId so both tasks polled reactions on the second comment only. The first task would never see its own approval reaction.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace let lastCommentId with Map<issueNumber, commentId>. waitForApproval() looks up by issueNumber.

findings.title: waitForApproval polled at fixed interval causing thundering-herd on GitHub reactions API
findings.detail: issue-commenter.ts waitForApproval() slept exactly opts.pollIntervalMs between every poll. With multiple concurrent tasks all started around the same time, they would fire their GitHub API requests in synchronized waves, increasing rate-limit pressure. Long HITL windows would also accumulate unnecessary API calls.
findings.fix_sketch: Apply exponential backoff (double each round, cap at 5 min) with ±25% jitter. Reset to base interval on transient API errors.

findings.title: resolveTaskIdFromMessage stub in daemon.ts had no comment explaining the intentional no-op
findings.detail: daemon.ts passed resolveTaskIdFromMessage: async () => null to createDiscordClient with no comment. A future reader would not know whether this was a bug (incomplete wiring) or intentional (routing via control-plane HTTP API). The Discord client already falls back to control-plane lookup on null returns.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a comment explaining the stub is intentional and documenting the fallback behavior.

findings.title: process.env['DISCORD_FALLBACK_CHANNEL_ID'] ?? undefined is a no-op redundant coalesce
findings.detail: daemon.ts line 93 used process.env['DISCORD_FALLBACK_CHANNEL_ID'] ?? undefined. process.env values are already string | undefined; the ?? undefined coalesces undefined to undefined, which is identical to just using process.env['DISCORD_FALLBACK_CHANNEL_ID'] directly.
